name: btn
summary: Check whether a button is held down.
note: Use indices 0–3 for left, right, up, and down; 4 is B and 5 is A. In the editor preview, Z is A and X is B.

name: btnp
summary: React to a button press, with held-button repeat.
note: A held button repeats after 15 update ticks and then every four ticks. Use btn() for continuous movement.

name: spr
signature: spr(id, x, y [, w, h, flip_x, flip_y])
summary: Draw a sprite from your sheet.
note: Sprite cells are 8×8 pixels. Position is the top-left corner; width and height are in cells. Color 0 is transparent by default. Create the artwork in the Sprites workspace first.

name: sspr
signature: sspr(sx, sy, sw, sh, dx, dy [, dw, dh, flip_x, flip_y])
summary: Draw a rectangular part of the sprite sheet.
note: Source coordinates and sizes are in pixels. Scaling or arbitrary crops require the bitmap renderer; aligned, unscaled rectangles may use hardware sprites.

name: sget
summary: Read a palette index from the sprite sheet.
note: This reads authored sheet pixels, not the finished screen.

name: sset
summary: Change a pixel in the sprite sheet.
note: This changes the game’s runtime copy. It does not save artwork back to your project. Hardware rendering requires bounded mutation placement; see the renderer contract.

name: fget
summary: Read a sprite’s flags.
note: With a flag index, reads that bit; without it, returns the flag byte. Flags are useful for labeling solid or collectible tiles.

name: fset
summary: Change a sprite’s flags.
note: A flag affects the logical sprite and later map filtering. Runtime mutation can change AUTO renderer selection.

name: map
signature: map() / map(bg [, cx, cy, x, y, w, h, mask])
summary: Draw the tile maps you created in the editor.
note: map() draws all authored non-empty planes, back to front. With arguments, the first is always a literal BG0–BG3 layer. Do not mix automatic and explicit forms. Source-cell offsets contribute to world positions; read the map contract before scrolling a subsection.

name: mget
summary: Read the sprite ID in a map cell.
note: Map coordinates are in 8×8 cells. The two-argument form uses BG0. Invalid coordinates or absent planes return 0.

name: mset
signature: mset(x, y, id) / mset(bg, x, y, id)
summary: Replace a map cell while the game runs.
note: The three-argument form edits BG0. Runtime edits are not saved into project files. Invalid coordinates are ignored.

name: camera
summary: Move the view without moving your game objects.
note: The camera position is subtracted from drawing coordinates. camera() resets the view. Keep world coordinates separate from screen coordinates.

name: cls
summary: Clear the screen for a new frame.
note: Colors are palette indices. In Aurora, 24 is dark blue and 15 is white. Put one unconditional cls() at the start of _draw() for hardware-renderer eligibility.

name: print
summary: Draw text or a number on the screen.
note: This explicit four-argument form is the easiest to start with. Separate labels and numeric values to keep them eligible for hardware rendering. Text uses a 6×8 cell font; Mode 0 has additional glyph and object limits.

name: pset
summary: Set one screen pixel.
note: Screen coordinates start at (0, 0) in the top-left. The screen is 240 pixels wide and 160 high.

name: pget
summary: Read a color from the composed screen.
note: The result reflects drawing that has already happened. Use sget() to inspect the sprite sheet instead.

name: line
summary: Draw a straight line between two points.
note: The current camera and clipping rectangle apply to the line.

name: rect
summary: Draw a rectangle outline.
note: The last two coordinates are the opposite corner, not width and height. The endpoints are inclusive.

name: rectfill
summary: Draw a filled rectangle.
note: Use opposite-corner coordinates. Drawing a filled rectangle is a bitmap-renderer operation.

name: circ
summary: Draw a circle outline.
note: The first two coordinates are the center. The radius is measured in pixels.

name: circfill
summary: Draw a filled circle.
note: Useful for quick prototypes and particles; this selects bitmap rendering.

name: color
summary: Set the default drawing color.
note: Explicit color arguments override the default. cls() does not change it.

name: cursor
summary: Set the text cursor position and optional color.
note: Explicitly positioned print() calls are usually clearer for a first game.

name: clip
summary: Limit drawing to a rectangle.
note: clip() restores full-screen drawing. Smaller clipping rectangles require Mode 4 in the current hardware-renderer subset.

name: pal
summary: Remap one palette color to another.
note: Remapping changes how colors are used or displayed. Mode 0 has placement and remapping restrictions; see the exact contract.

name: palt
summary: Control which sprite colors are transparent.
note: The default makes palette index 0 transparent in sprites and maps. Arbitrary transparent colors require Mode 4.

name: sfx
summary: Play a short sound-effect clip.
note: Create an SFX clip with this ID in Audio first, or use Coin Quest’s included clip 0. Default priority is 160. sfx(-1) stops gameplay-owned effects.

name: music
summary: Start a song from the Audio workspace.
note: Create a song with this ID first. music(-1) stops song-owned notes while leaving gameplay effects independent.

name: gba_note
summary: Play a hardware note using a saved sound.
note: Channels are 1–4. The sound must match the channel. Timed notes use 96 ticks per quarter note; zero duration sustains until stopped.

name: gba_stop
summary: Stop notes on a hardware channel.
note: Use channel numbers 1–4. This is a direct channel command; music and effects share these hardware channels.

name: flr
summary: Round down to an integer.
note: flr(-1.5) is -2, not -1. Use it when converting pixel coordinates into map cells.

name: ceil
summary: Round up to an integer.
note: ceil(-1.5) is -1. Numbers in mTile use 16:16 fixed point.

name: abs
summary: Get the distance of a number from zero.
note: abs(-8) is 8. Handy for simple collision checks.

name: sgn
summary: Return -1 for a negative number, or 1 otherwise.
note: sgn(0) returns 1.

name: min
summary: Choose the smaller of two numbers.
note: Use this to cap a value at an upper limit.

name: max
summary: Choose the larger of two numbers.
note: Use this to keep a value above a lower limit.

name: mid
summary: Choose the middle value of three numbers.
note: Putting a value between its lower and upper bounds clamps it to that range.

name: sin
summary: Get the vertical sine component of a turn.
note: Angles use turns, not degrees or radians. sin(0.25) is -1, matching a screen where Y increases downward.

name: cos
summary: Get the horizontal cosine component of a turn.
note: One complete turn is 1. cos(0) is 1.

name: atan2
summary: Find a direction angle in turns.
note: Uses the screen-coordinate convention shared with sin() and cos().

name: sqrt
summary: Find a square root.
note: Fixed-point precision is finite. Squared distances are often sufficient when comparing distances.

name: rnd
summary: Choose a pseudorandom number, or an item from a table.
note: The numeric form ranges from zero up to, but excluding, the limit. rnd() uses a limit of 1.

name: srand
summary: Set the random-number seed.
note: A fixed seed makes random sequences repeatable for testing.

name: add
summary: Append or insert a value into a list.
note: Lua list indices start at 1. Insertion shifts the existing elements.

name: del
summary: Remove the first matching value from a list.
note: Use deli() when you know the index rather than the value.

name: deli
summary: Remove an element by its list index.
note: With no index, removes the final element.

name: count
summary: Count list entries, optionally matching a value.
note: The optional value filters the count.

name: all
signature: for value in all(table) do ... end
summary: Visit each value in a list.
example:
for value in all({10, 20, 30}) do
  printh(value)
end
note: all() is iterator syntax here. Do not assign the iterator itself to a variable.

name: pairs
signature: for key, value in pairs(table) do ... end
summary: Visit a table’s keys and values.
example:
for key, value in pairs({score=5}) do
  printh(key)
end
note: Do not rely on a particular traversal order.

name: foreach
summary: Call a function for each list element.
example:
function show(value)
  printh(value)
end
foreach({10, 20}, show)
note: Use a named, statically bound callback. Read the foreach guide for mutation rules.

name: sub
summary: Take a section of a string.
note: Indices start at 1 and the final index is inclusive. String operations are byte-oriented.

name: tostr
summary: Convert a value to text.
note: For Mode 0 text, print numeric values directly instead of passing a converted string.

name: tonum
summary: Convert numeric text to a number.
note: Check input before using a conversion in game logic.

name: chr
summary: Create a one-byte string from a character code.
note: 65 is uppercase A. This is a byte operation, not a Unicode conversion.

name: ord
summary: Read a byte’s numeric character code.
note: Indices start at 1.

name: time
summary: Read elapsed game time in seconds.
note: t() is an alias. This is game time, not the computer’s wall clock.

name: t
summary: Read elapsed game time in seconds.
note: An alias for time().

name: stat
summary: Read runtime performance counters.
note: stat(1) is the previous tick’s share of the roughly 30 Hz frame budget: 1 means the entire budget. It is not host CPU percentage. See the performance guide for other counters.

name: printh
summary: Write a value to the preview debug log.
note: Useful for observing game logic while running in the editor’s instrumented preview.

name: band
summary: Bitwise AND.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: bor
summary: Bitwise OR.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: bxor
summary: Bitwise exclusive OR.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: bnot
summary: Invert the bits of a number.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: shl
summary: Shift bits left.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: shr
summary: Shift bits right with sign extension.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: lshr
summary: Shift bits right without sign extension.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: rotl
summary: Rotate bits left.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.

name: rotr
summary: Rotate bits right.
note: These operate on the 32-bit fixed-point representation. Keep bit operations separate from ordinary arithmetic until you are comfortable with that representation.
